text:
maria: Heads up — consoles are super slow for a bunch of customers since the 03:15 deploy. Charts timeout / spinner for ~8-12s, even on small orgs. Seeing lots of network retries.
kevin: I noticed realtime metrics spike too. Any specific page or all dashboards?
maria: Mainly the overview and query heatmap. Repro steps: open org A dashboard, click time range, charts hang. Devtools shows an extra 1.1MB JS chunk loaded on every route called `telemetry-trace-lite.v2.js`.
ryan: Hmm that was added in the telemetry client upgrade we pushed in the same deploy (trace-lite v2). It changed how we instrument fetch — now it injects a wrapper on the global fetch which pulls the trace lib on first use.
alisa: Also saw backend routing change around the same time — chart data requests are now being proxied via the routing-policy service and some requests are going to eu-west for NA users. Cross-region + cold trace lib fetch could explain the 8s.
maria: Waterfall: initial HTML 150ms, main bundle 180ms, then telemetry-trace-lite.v2.js 1.1s, then first chart data request gets routed to eu-west and DNS/latency ~200ms, but subsequent retries/timeouts push visible render to 8s.
kevin: Can we confirm if a simple revert of telemetry client stops the extra chunk load? If so we can hotfix quickly.
ryan: Locally I toggled telemetry_v2=false and the trace lib doesn't load — charts render in ~220ms. So yes that's the main contributor.
dave: We should also fix the routing policy rule causing EU affinity for some NA orgs. I suspect a fallback priority change in routing-config where weight for local-region fell to 0.
kevin: Ok plan: 1) feature-flag the telemetry client rollback for canary, 2) patch routing-policy to restore region affinity, 3) increase telemetry sampling to avoid pulling lib often until we rework onboarding.
maria: +1. For immediate mitigation can we block the trace-lite chunk from being preloaded? It seems to be eagerly fetched when a small widget mounts.
dave: We can add a temporary webpack rule to lazy-load the lib behind a flag and strip any prefetch/link headers. But that requires deploy. Faster is a flag in the CDN edge to 403 that path — ugly but quick.
kevin: Let's do the flag rollback first. Ryan — can you create a rollout to flip telemetry_v2=false for 100% of prod? Use rollout-service:```
# rollout-cli
rollout set telemetry_v2 --env=prod --value=false --strategy=immediate
```
ryan: Doing it now. Starting canary to 10% -> 50% -> 100%. deploy-bot: "canary-deploy started by ryan — service: console-frontend — id: canary-2263456790"
obs-bot: "Alert: p95 chart render time spiked from 420ms -> 4.8s at 03:17 across eu-west & us-west"
kevin: After canary at 50% I still see a small tail where old sessions keep the chunk. We should also clear the client side aggressive prefetch that was added last week: in `prefetch-middleware` we set Link: <.../telemetry-trace-lite.v2.js>; rel=prefetch. Remove that header for now.
maria: I pushed a tiny PR to remove the prefetch header (build pipeline) — PR #3251. If CI passes we can merge and include in the same rollback deploy.
ryan: Can confirm that once telemetry_v2=false and prefetch removed locally, chart time goes back to normal (~200-300ms).
kevin: Routing policy patch: restore default region weight to 100 for local-region in routing-config and add a test that simulates heavy cold-start to ensure we don't regress. Alisa, can you own the routing change?
alisa: On it. I found the config diff — `regionAffinity: { defaultWeight: 0 }` accidentally merged. Reverting to `100` and adding a unit test. PR #3252.
dave: Also recommend we increase telemetry sampling to 0.1% cluster-wide so we don't frequently pull client libs for low-value sessions. We'll revisit after we fully vet trace-lite memory/size cost.
kevin: Agreed. After rollback + routing fix + header removal we'll run a staged deploy and monitor console p95 for 30m. If stable, mark incident resolved and schedule a postmortem.
maria: Post-deploy numbers: before fix p95=4.8s, after telemetry flag rolled out to 100% and prefetch removed p95=280ms. Great.
ryan: Logging follow-up: capture the trace id when trace-lite loads so we can correlate which sessions pulled it. Add an obs event: `trace_lib_loaded` with sampleRate 1%.
dave: Also add a dashboard card showing chunk size over time and origin header so we can detect future regressions quickly.
kevin: I'll create an ops runbook entry for "slow charts after frontend deploy" with checklist: check telemetry chunk, check prefetch header, check routing-config weights.
maria: Thanks team. We'll leave telemetry_v2 disabled until we've validated a smaller bundle or on-demand load without blocking charts.
kevin: Assigning owners: ryan => telemetry rollback monitoring, alisa => routing-policy fix, dave => chunk-dashboard + sampling plan, maria => validation and postmortem doc.
ryan: Rollout finished: deploy-bot: "canary-deploy complete — console-frontend — id: canary-2263456790 — status: success"
obs-bot: "Metric update: chart p95 back to baseline (now 280ms)."
maria: I'll open the postmortem draft in #postmortems and link these PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:"
